calls.head: Penalties could cost the Islanders
calls.body: The Hurricanes’ power play is near the top of the league, and the Islanders’ kill is one of the worst. Every trip to the box hurts the Islanders more than most.

calls.head: The Hurricanes should tilt the ice
calls.body: The Hurricanes have been the league’s best at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Islanders around the middle. Expect the Hurricanes to spend more of the night in the Islanders’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

surprises.head: The Islanders picked Carolina’s defense apart
surprises.body: Carolina usually gives up some of the league’s most dangerous shots. Even by those standards, this was a night of good looks: the Islanders’ shots at 5-on-5 had a 9.3% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.3% (about 6.9% against Carolina) and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 20 games.

story.head: The Hurricanes edge the Islanders
paras: Logan Stankoven and Jesperi Kotkaniemi scored less than three minutes apart early in the first to put the Hurricanes up 2-0. It was a busy second period. Mitchell Chaffee scored his first goal for the Islanders early in the period to get the Islanders on the board. Brayden Schenn made it 2-2 just over two minutes later, and Andrei Svechnikov restored the Hurricanes’ lead a minute later. Victor Eklund tied it up for the Islanders late in the second, but that was the last goal the Islanders would get. William Carrier put the Hurricanes ahead for good with just over five minutes left, and Jalen Chatfield sealed it into the empty net with just under a minute left.

The Hurricanes outshot the Islanders 39-27, but the Islanders’ looks were better, so the chances came out about even. Brandon Bussi made 24 saves for the Canes, and Semyon Varlamov stopped 34 of 38 at the other end. By our Swing measure, K'Andre Miller had the best night of anyone.

Juuso Välimäki and Kyle MacLean picked up ten-minute misconducts. Neither power play scored: the Hurricanes killed all four Islanders power plays, and the Islanders killed both of Carolina’s. The Hurricanes moved to 13-3-2 and took sole possession of first in the NHL in both points and points percentage, while the Islanders dropped to 7-6-2, fifth in the Metropolitan.

items.text: Jackson Blake has a point in eight straight games.
The Hurricanes have beaten the Islanders five straight times, going back to the 2024-25 season.
William Carrier scored his first goal of the season, his first since Apr 7 (20 games played since).

The Islanders were without Mathew Barzal, Matias Maccelli, Alexander Romanov and others. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Ducks were missing more at the time.
